title: Data Centers and Local Housing Markets
abstract: I study how large data center openings affect local residential real estate markets. Using an event study design with distance-based treatment rings (0.5, 1, and 2 miles from facility locations), I find that data center openings generate positive house price effects within a half-mile radius, consistent with a local employment demand channel. Effects on rents, migration flows, and consumer spending are examined to distinguish supply- from demand-side mechanisms.

title: Flood Risk Discounting in Residential Mortgage Pricing
abstract: We examine whether lenders price physical climate risk into mortgage interest rates and LTV ratios using property-level flood zone data matched to loan origination records. We find that flood zone designation lowers loan-to-value ratios by 3–5 percentage points at origination but has limited effects on rates, suggesting lenders primarily manage climate exposure through collateral haircuts rather than risk-adjusted pricing.
